_readme: Every word the conversation panel says on its own, before the AI says anything. Edit the strings, reload, done — no code. What the AI itself knows about Elliot is NOT here: that is server/persona.ts, which is the only file the model ever reads, and it is kept off the client on purpose. 'pick' is the opening choice: the panel starts on three options and nothing can be typed until one is chosen — watch the film, get the TL;DR card, or book a call. The first two are handed to the world (main.ts raises the screen, or shows the card); the third is a conversation, and 'pick.bookOpener' is the line sent as the visitor's first words when they choose it, the way a chip is; 'pick.bookGreeting' is Elliot's reply to it, shown at once rather than generated (the server signs it as its own, in /api/live), because the model's answer to that line is always the same question and the wait for it was the visitor's first impression of the conversation. Change the two together: the AI reads both as the start of the transcript. 'pick.filmAgain' replaces 'pick.film' once the film has been watched. 'pick.back' is the one chip in the booking conversation, and it returns to the three choices. The interview — 'questions', 'pick.talk', 'pick.toTalk', 'pick.toBook' — is parked: the code for it is still in chat.ts and the server still answers the 'talk' brief, but the choice is not offered. 'questions' are the interview's chips, in order. Only a few are on screen at a time (chat.ts decides how many); when one is asked it leaves and the next in this list takes its place, so the list can be long without the panel being a menu. Each one is sent to the AI verbatim as if the visitor had typed it, so they read as questions a person would actually ask, in the second person. 'fallback' is what Elliot says when the AI cannot be reached, by cause; none of those lines are generated either. 'live' labels the short lines under the header that are read live from his own accounts as the panel opens — Spotify, GitHub, Strava, WHOOP, Calendly — each one naming its source in small type and absent when there is nothing to show.
questions: What did you actually do at Cassidy?
What are you looking for next?
What’s a weakness you’re working on?
What do you do outside of work?
What are you listening to right now?

pick.label: What would you like to do?
pick.film: Watch a short film Elliot made about himself
pick.digest: Get the TL;DR version of the film
pick.bookOpener: I’d like to book a call with Elliot.
pick.bookGreeting: Happy to. What days or times suit you this week or next?
pick.toTalk: Ask me about my work instead

fallback.unconfigured: I’ve lost my voice — the AI behind me isn’t switched on right now. The real Elliot is one email away: elliotgreenbaum@gmail.com.
fallback.busy: Give me a moment — too many questions at once. Try that one again in a minute.
fallback.error: Something went wrong on my end. Ask again, or email the real Elliot at elliotgreenbaum@gmail.com.
